The Family Care Stress-Points Checklist

What to review, ask and write down while the arrangement is working.

Download PDF

You look after your husband, and it works, more or less. The list of what you do has grown one task at a time, and nobody has sat down to look at it. This page is a way to look. Check what you've done. Anything unchecked is something for a quiet hour, not a verdict on how things are going.

Review

Ask

Write down

What this checklist doesn't do

It helps you look, ask and write things down. It doesn't say whether the arrangement is working, and it doesn't tell you that anything has to change. A checklist can't answer either of those, and this one doesn't try.

Ready for the next step?

You've looked over the week, asked around and started a list. The care interview goes through your husband's situation and the help around him area by area, including the parts that feel too ordinary to mention, and turns your answers into a Family Care Profile you can bring to any care conversation.

Create Your Free Family Care Profile ›

Where this comes from

Items marked 1 follow the National Institute on Aging's advice to check in regularly with the person being cared for and everyone who helps. The item marked 2 follows the Family Caregiver Alliance's point that one family meeting rarely covers everything. The rest come from the Family Care Roadmap's own working list for this step.

  1. National Institute on Aging, Sharing Caregiving Responsibilities
  2. Family Caregiver Alliance, Holding a Family Meeting
